## Taste, built in.

Every brief is matched against a design library distilled from open-source design work, and every version is checked as it’s built. You get a point of view, not an average.

### How every version is reviewed

### Checked on every version

- Exactly one main headline, with header, main and footer landmarks

- Alt text on every image, a name on every button, a label on every field

- Menus, dialogs and toggles wired to real targets, with a menu for phones

- Motion that respects reduced-motion settings

- No lorem ipsum and none of the stock buzzwords

- Set up to scale on phones, with a page title and a search description

- On full sites, every link checked against the site’s pages and anchors, and dead ends repaired

The design library is distilled from open-source work by anthropics ( anthropics/skills on GitHub, opens in a new tab) , nextlevelbuilder ( nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill on GitHub, opens in a new tab) , VoltAgent ( VoltAgent/awesome-design-md on GitHub, opens in a new tab) , superdesigndev ( superdesigndev/superdesign-skill on GitHub, opens in a new tab) , greensock ( greensock/gsap-skills on GitHub, opens in a new tab) and vercel-labs ( vercel-labs/agent-skills on GitHub, opens in a new tab) .

## Questions

A sentence is enough: what you’re launching, who it’s for, and anything you care about. You can also speak instead of typing, and attach your logo, product photos, a PDF deck or a notes file. Marquee reads them and puts your real images on the page.

Nothing is picked from a gallery. Each brief is matched to a design direction, palette and type pairing for that kind of business, then the page is designed and written from scratch for it. Then the page is critiqued against design rules for generic-design tells and the weak spots are rebuilt, with a second and third round when the first finds more than a few problems.
